text:
dan: quick thought - if autofallback keeps flipping model variants during noisy upstream blips we could end up thrashing pools. need a safety throttle + stabilization window.
lee: agreed. propose two primitives: (1) hysteresis (percent change required to flip back) (2) stabilization "hold" after any autofallback for N minutes.
maya: UX: show a small timeline in the rollback panel with the last 15m signal and a marker where the decision would apply. operators can scrub to see affected requests.
clare: also useful to have an "auto-suppress" band: if error rate fluctuates inside [low, high] do not trigger repeatedly. basically a dead-zone.
ops-bot: notice: [AUTOFALLBACK] service=embed-svc policy=stability-v2 signal=latency_p95=650ms trigger=policy_eval id=df-20260401-09
tom: policy DSL idea - keep it compact but expressive. example:
```yaml
trigger:
  metric: p95_latency_ms
  op: '>'
  value: 600
  window: 120s
stabilization:
  hold_for: 8m           # no new auto-switches for this pool
  hysteresis_pct: 12    # require 12% improvement to revert
  max_auto_switches: 2  # per hour
noise_filter:
  deadzone_low: 550
  deadzone_high: 650
telemetry:
  attach_decision_to_requests_for: 3m
  trace_sampling: 0.05
  audit_store_ttl: 24h
```
lee: love the yaml. add `require_manual_over` for percent impact - if a switch would move >30% traffic require human confirm.
dan: telemetry: we should emit three events: autofallback.requested, autofallback.executed, autofallback.cancelled. each must include decision_id, pool_id, policy_hash, and snapshot_metrics. joins with traces.
maya: on the console side show a compact diff: before vs after routing table (percent per variant), estimated cost delta, and links to 5 sampled requests that informed the decision.
clare: on audit - exportable JSON with decision_id, timestamps, sample_request_ids, evaluation_snapshot, and operator comment. also allow owners to annotate after the fact.
dan: edge case: what about overlapping decisions from multiple policies? e.g. quota-based fallback + safety fallback. we need policy priority and a pre-flight check that prevents conflicting concurrent actions.
lee: yes enforce a lock per pool while a decision is in stabilization. if another policy wants to act, it either queues or annotates. show pending decisions in UI.
maya: small UI nicety: gray out the manual rollback button during stabilization, but allow "force" with a required typed confirmation and audit note.
tom: implementation notes: platform should evaluate policy candidate actions in an isolated dry-run mode and compute impact delta before commit. return impact_score and affected_pct to UI.
ops-bot: recommended playbook entry: "Investigate autofallback oscillation" added and assigned to dan.
dan: action items: (1) platform: add hysteresis + hold_for + max_auto_switches to policy schema (lee/tom), (2) telemetry: decision events + attach decision_id to requests for configured duration (maya/telemetry), (3) console: timeline preview + impact diff + forced-override flow (maya/clare). i'll draft a one-pager and drop a prototype next week. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
